meta.note: Week of June 22 — broken rib recovery protocol: all workouts are low-impact, no twisting, no overhead, no high-impact cardio. Hit protein at every meal and finish dinner 2.5–3 hrs before bed.

monday.label: Monday

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
exercises.cue: Chest up, knees tracking over toes, sit back into the squat. No weight needed — focus on depth and control. Safe for broken rib.

exercises.name: Walking Lunges (10 lb dumbbells)
exercises.cue: Step long, 90-degree knee angle. Hold dumbbells at sides — no overhead. Torso upright and neutral spine.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Glute Bridge
exercises.cue: Band above knees, lie on back, drive through heels, full hip extension at top. Zero rib stress.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust (off couch)
exercises.cue: Upper back on couch edge, drive through heel. Full hip extension. Glute isolation — no core flexion required.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Clamshell
exercises.cue: Band above knees, side-lying. Open like a clamshell. Fires hip abductors. Gentle breathing throughout.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raises
exercises.cue: Full range of motion, pause at top. Use wall for balance. Safe and effective — no rib involvement.

monday.recovery: Gentle lower body stretch — hip flexors, glutes, calves. No twisting or reaching overhead.

tuesday.label: Tuesday

exercises.name: Brisk Walk
exercises.cue: Purposeful pace, arms relaxed at sides. No arm swinging overhead. Great for cortisol reduction and rib healing — gentle movement increases circulation to the injury site.

exercises.name: Elevated Child's Pose
exercises.cue: Start on all fours, lower upper body with hips raised, hands flat, head relaxed. Widens space between your knees if rib cage pressure is felt. One of the safest stretches for broken ribs.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow (very gentle)
exercises.cue: On all fours. MINIMAL range — only go as far as pain-free. This gently mobilizes the thoracic spine and promotes healing without stressing the fracture.

exercises.name: Legs Up the Wall (Viparita Karani)
exercises.cue: Lie on back, legs resting vertically on wall. Zero effort. Reduces leg swelling from hospital shifts, lowers cortisol, and takes all pressure off the rib cage.

exercises.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
exercises.cue: One hand on belly, one on chest. Breathe so only the belly hand rises. Do NOT let chest expand — this protects the rib and is clinically recommended to prevent lung complications after rib fractures.

exercises.name: Seated Lateral Twist (gentle)
exercises.cue: Seated in chair, arms crossed on chest. TINY gentle rotation only — stop at first hint of pain. 3x per day recommended to prevent spinal stiffness during rib recovery.

tuesday.recovery: Legs up wall 5 min post-walk. Diaphragmatic breathing 3x today — therapeutic for rib fracture healing.

wednesday.label: Wednesday

exercises.name: Pool Walking — Chest-Deep Water
exercises.cue: Walk the length of the pool at a brisk pace. Arms move naturally at sides — do NOT swing overhead. Water resistance gives a full-body workout. Safe for broken rib: no torso rotation, no impact.

exercises.name: Aqua Jogging (with or without belt)
exercises.cue: Jog in place or across the pool in deep water. Upright posture, arms at sides. This mimics running's cardio benefit with zero impact on ribs. Heart rate 60–70% max.

exercises.name: Flutter Kick with Kickboard
exercises.cue: Hold kickboard in front (arms extended). Kick only — NO freestyle arm stroke to avoid rib rotation. Excellent lower body cardio and cardiovascular training.

exercises.name: Pool Walking — Side Steps
exercises.cue: Face the lane line and side-step across. Works hip abductors and keeps heart rate up without any twisting.

exercises.name: Gentle Backstroke (if pain-free)
exercises.cue: Backstroke distributes force more evenly than freestyle. Only attempt if zero pain. Stop immediately if any rib discomfort. Skip entirely in week 1.

wednesday.recovery: 5 min float on back after pool session — zero effort, nervous system reset. Legs up wall + diaphragmatic breathing at home.

thursday.label: Thursday

workout.name: Home Lower Body Circuit B — Glute Focus

exercises.name: Banded Glute Bridge
exercises.cue: Band above knees. On your back — zero rib stress. Drive through heels, squeeze hard at top. The safest glute exercise possible with a broken rib.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat (20 lb med ball)
exercises.cue: Hold med ball at chest level. Chest up, neutral spine. Do NOT press ball overhead at any point. Focus on depth and control.

exercises.name: Step-Ups (10 lb dumbbells)
exercises.cue: Use a sturdy chair or step. Hold dumbbells at sides — no overhead. Drive through the front heel. Great cardio + glute work with zero rib impact.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Lateral Walk
exercises.cue: Band just above knees. Slight squat position. Side-step — keep tension in band throughout. Hip abductor strength protects knees during running return.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Raise (lower body only)
exercises.cue: Lie flat, hands under hips for support. Raise both legs to 90° slowly, lower slowly. NO sit-up component — back stays flat on the floor throughout. Stop if any rib tightness.

exercises.name: Calf Raises (weighted, 10 lb DBs)
exercises.cue: Hold dumbbells at sides, rise on toes. Full range. Prevents calf tightness during rib recovery when running is paused.

thursday.recovery: Lower body stretch routine — hip flexors, glutes, hamstrings. No twisting. Legs up wall if legs feel heavy.

friday.label: Friday

exercises.name: Outdoor Walk
exercises.cue: Easy purposeful pace. Arms relaxed. This is one of the most healing activities for a broken rib — promotes circulation, prevents pneumonia risk, and reduces cortisol. No hiking or uneven terrain.

exercises.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
exercises.cue: Belly-only breathing. Do 3 sessions today spaced throughout the day — morning, post-lunch, evening. Clinically recommended to keep lungs clear during rib fracture recovery.

exercises.name: Seated Lateral Twists
exercises.cue: Arms crossed on chest, seated. Tiny range of motion — only as far as totally pain-free. Prevents spinal stiffness. 3x today.

exercises.name: Legs Up the Wall
exercises.cue: Full rest. Reduces leg swelling from shift work. Zero rib involvement. Do this in the evening before bed.

meals.recipe: 2 Homemade Energy Balls

friday.recovery: Diaphragmatic breathing 3x today. Warm shower on tight areas before bed — also reduces cortisol and improves reflux.

saturday.label: Saturday

exercises.name: Pool Walking — Chest-Deep Water
exercises.cue: Brisk walking laps. Arms at sides. If this week 1 felt good, push the pace slightly. Still no freestyle arm stroke.

exercises.name: Aqua Jogging Intervals
exercises.cue: 1 min at hard aqua jog effort, 30 sec easy walk. This is your cardio interval session for the week — mimics OTF effort but with zero rib stress. Progress from Wed if pain-free.

exercises.name: Flutter Kick with Kickboard
exercises.cue: Two more lengths than Wednesday. Legs only. Excellent for cardiovascular conditioning and lower body strength while protecting the rib.

exercises.name: Pool Walking — Side Steps + Backward Walk
exercises.cue: Side steps + backward walking. Works different muscle groups and keeps heart rate elevated without any twisting.

exercises.name: 5 min Float — Back
exercises.cue: End every pool session floating on your back. Buoyancy decompresses the spine, rhythm of water lowers cortisol measurably. This is your nervous system reset — mandatory.

saturday.recovery: 5 min back float after pool session. Full lower body stretch at home. Epsom salt bath tonight if available — reduces DOMS and cortisol.

sunday.label: Sunday

exercises.name: Gentle Walk (optional)
exercises.cue: Only if feeling good. Easy pace, flat ground. This is a full rest day — hosting dinner tonight, so conserve energy.

exercises.name: Full Stretch Routine
exercises.cue: Lower body focus. Hip flexors, glutes, calves, hamstrings. No twisting. Hold each 30–45 sec. Breathe deeply — parasympathetic activation soothes GI and lowers cortisol.

exercises.name: Lymphatic Drainage (legs)
exercises.cue: Especially valuable after a week of shifts. Light upward strokes from ankle toward knee, knee toward groin. Finish with legs elevated 5–10 min. Great before hosting.

exercises.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
exercises.cue: Belly-only breathing. Do morning, afternoon, and evening. Therapeutic for rib healing all week — don't skip on rest days.
